notes: Added for relation-property coverage (CRITERIA Rule 12). The relation is 'lobe_of' (new in this topic), declared a subproperty of 'part_of' and with the role chain lobe_of ∘ part_of ⊑ part_of, so its two determinate queries test subproperty (the temporal lobe is part of the liver) and a declared chain (liver → digestive system). Derivability very unlikely: 'the temporal lobe of the brain' is stated thousands of times and follows from nothing firmer. The edit crosses organs on purpose (the liver really has lobes). Background beliefs: structures that sit in the temporal lobe may be stored under the brain by name (they stay) or under the temporal lobe (they move with it), as the Eiffel Tower under Paris or under 'the capital'. Two independent choices give 4 worlds; the w1-style worlds, where they stay in the brain, are probably likelier for the hippocampus (Decision 4: kept). Not used: 'Is the temporal lobe part of the cerebrum?' (the cerebrum is the brain's main part, so a model might keep it by a separate stored fact; unclear). Names: 颞叶 ('temple lobe') and 'lóbulo temporal' do not encode the organ. Near query: the occipital lobe and visual cortex are untouched by the edit. Formal check (FINDINGS C2): the original 'no' answers of q0 and q1 rest on the brain being part of the central nervous system and on the brain and liver, and the central nervous system and digestive system, sharing no structure; all three are now bridges with checks.
